Despite balance sheet reduction, the Bank of Japan remains the dominant force in Japan's bond market:

The Bank of Japan now holds ~46% of Japanese government bonds (JGBs), down -8 percentage points from its 2023 peak and its lowest proportion since 2021.

Yet, the BoJ still holds more JGBs than banks, life insurers, pension funds, and foreign investors combined.

By comparison, the BoJ owned just ~10% of JGBs in 2013.

This comes despite BoJ holdings of JGBs dropping -$310 billion over the 12 months ending in July, their largest decline in history.

This brought the BoJ's total JGB holdings down to ~$3.3 trillion, its lowest since 2020, but still +400% above 2012 levels.

Profit margins for Technology, Media, & Telecom (TMT) stocks are up to a record 24%.

This is still below the 2007 peak before the Financial Crisis started and below the 2021 high.

As a result, tech profit margins are now ~2.7x higher than the rest of the market.

BREAKING: China's central bank officially bought +20 tonnes of gold in August, matching its largest monthly purchase since October 2023.

This follows +20 tonnes and +15 tonnes acquired in July and June, respectively, and marks its 22nd consecutive monthly gold purchase.

So far in 2026, China has officially added +80 tonnes to its gold reserves, lifting total holdings to a record 2,387 tonnes.

By comparison, in full-year 2025, China increased its official gold reserves by a total of +29 tonnes.

In troy ounces, China added ~650,000 ounces to its reserves last month, taking its total holdings to a record 76.73 million ounces.

China continues to stockpile gold at a historic pace.
